config.title: Build A B test assignment utility

intro.title: Build A B test assignment utility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple A/B test assignment utility that randomly assigns users to either a 'control' or 'variant' group. You'll learn how to use JavaScript's Math.random() function to generate random numbers and apply conditional logic to make assignments. The main technologies involved are basic JavaScript functions, variables, and if/else statements. By the end, you'll have a working utility that can be integrated into web projects to test different features or designs.
intro.usecase: A/B test assignment utilities are foundational for data-driven product development, enabling developers to scientifically evaluate feature impact. In real-world applications, this pattern is used to split user traffic between different versions of a webpage, a checkout flow, or a promotional banner to measure which performs better. For example, an e-commerce dashboard might use this utility to test whether a red 'Buy Now' button converts more sales than a blue one, or a news website might test different headline placements. Implementing this utility allows developers to make informed decisions based on user behavior rather than assumptions, directly influencing product metrics like engagement and revenue.

objectives: Construct a function to generate a random user ID for test assignment
Implement a utility function that assigns users to variant A or B based on a consistent hash
Configure a test configuration object to define experiment names and variant weights
Initialize a state object to track the assigned variant for a user across multiple experiments
Manipulate the DOM to display the assigned variant and simulate different user experiences
Integrate the assignment utility into a simple webpage to demonstrate A/B test functionality
Control the test assignment by adjusting variant weights and observing the distribution
